
### `GET /api/organizations/:organization_id/dead-letters`

Inspect the tenant's dead letters by opaque record ID.

What ended up here after every retry. Records are addressed by opaque ID and carry no recipient PII.

- **URL:** `https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/:organization_id/dead-letters`
- **Auth:** `organization` — Session plus X-Organization-Id membership, or a scoped API key that determines the organization.

**Path parameters**

- `organization_id` (string, required) — Active organization ID. It must match the organization your session header or API key resolves to.

**Response `200`**

- `items` (object[]) — One record per dead letter: origin, reason, when it failed.

**Errors**

- `401` — No session, no API key, or the credential does not resolve to this organization.
- `403` — The identity is valid but lacks the required role or scope for this operation.
- `404` — The resource does not exist in this organization. Another tenant's ID answers the same 404 — the API never confirms that it exists elsewhere.

**Example**

```sh
curl -s https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/$ORG/dead-letters -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Organization-Id: $ORG"
```

### `POST /api/organizations/:organization_id/dead-letters/:record_id/replay`

Replay one campaign or webhook dead letter, by name.

One record at a time, addressed explicitly. There is no "replay everything": a bulk replay of an unknown set is how a bad hour becomes a bad day.

- **URL:** `https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/:organization_id/dead-letters/:record_id/replay`
- **Auth:** `organization_campaign_write` — Active organization identity with campaign:write permission. Campaign launches require Idempotency-Key.

**Path parameters**

- `organization_id` (string, required) — Active organization ID. It must match the organization your session header or API key resolves to.
- `record_id` (string, required) — Dead-letter record ID from the dead-letter listing.

**Body example**

```json
{}
```

**Response `200`**

- `dead_letter` (object) — The record with its new replay state.

**Errors**

- `401` — No session, no API key, or the credential does not resolve to this organization.
- `403` — The identity is valid but lacks the required role or scope for this operation.
- `404` — The resource does not exist in this organization. Another tenant's ID answers the same 404 — the API never confirms that it exists elsewhere.
- `409` — The record was already replayed or is not replayable.

**Example**

```sh
curl -s -XPOST https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/$ORG/dead-letters/$RECORD/replay -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Organization-Id: $ORG" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'
```

## Billing

### `GET /api/billing`

Read the versioned trial, pass and top-up catalog, plus the x402 network in force.

Public and unauthenticated: an agent should be able to learn what things cost before deciding whether to sign up at all.

- **URL:** `https://commsharbor.com/api/billing`
- **Auth:** `none` — Public endpoint. No tenant data is returned.

**Response `200`**

Structure: `BillingPublic`.

- `catalog` (BillingCatalog) — Plans and prices in force. → see `BillingCatalog` under **Structures**.
- `payment` (PlanoX402) — x402 configuration: network, asset, facilitator and where to pay. → see `PlanoX402` under **Structures**.
- `invite_only` (bool) — Whether new organizations require an invitation.

**Example**

```sh
curl -s https://commsharbor.com/api/billing
```

### `GET /api/organizations/:organization_id/billing`

Read this organization's entitlement, quota allocation and expiration warning.

Read this before a bulk send: `state` says how many sends remain and `warning` says when the entitlement runs out.

- **URL:** `https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/:organization_id/billing`
- **Auth:** `organization` — Session plus X-Organization-Id membership, or a scoped API key that determines the organization.

**Path parameters**

- `organization_id` (string, required) — Active organization ID. It must match the organization your session header or API key resolves to.

**Response `200`**

Structure: `BillingTenant`.

- `catalog` (BillingCatalog) — Plans and prices in force. → see `BillingCatalog` under **Structures**.
- `state` (object) — Current entitlement: what is active, how many sends remain and when it expires.
- `warning` (object, may be null) — Expiration or exhaustion warning, when one applies.
- `payment` (PlanoX402) — x402 configuration for paying. → see `PlanoX402` under **Structures**.

**Errors**

- `401` — No session, no API key, or the credential does not resolve to this organization.
- `403` — The identity is valid but lacks the required role or scope for this operation.
- `404` — The resource does not exist in this organization. Another tenant's ID answers the same 404 — the API never confirms that it exists elsewhere.

**Example**

```sh
curl -s https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/$ORG/billing -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Organization-Id: $ORG"
```

### `POST /api/organizations/:organization_id/billing/purchases/:action`

Request a pass or a top-up. While live checkout is off, this answers with an x402 challenge.

The response is a standard **402 with `accepts[]`** unless `catalog.checkout_live` is true — nobody is charged by accident. The Idempotency-Key makes a retry safe: the same logical purchase never grants entitlement twice.

- **URL:** `https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/:organization_id/billing/purchases/:action`
- **Auth:** `organization_admin` — Human organization member with the required role; API keys cannot manage credentials or membership.

**Path parameters**

- `organization_id` (string, required) — Active organization ID. It must match the organization your session header or API key resolves to.
- `action` (string, required) — Which purchase to request. Values: `pass`, `topup`.

**Headers**

- `Idempotency-Key` (string, required) — Stable key for this logical purchase. A replay returns the same state and grants nothing extra.
- `X-PAYMENT` (string) — Standard x402 payment payload, when live checkout is explicitly enabled.

**Body example**

```json
{}
```

**Response `200`**

- `replayed` (bool) — True when this key had already been used and nothing new was granted.
- `state` (object) — The entitlement after the request: what is active, what remains, when it expires.

**Errors**

- `400` — Missing Idempotency-Key, or an action other than `pass`/`topup`.
- `401` — No session, no API key, or the credential does not resolve to this organization.
- `402` — Payment required — the body carries `accepts[]`. This is the normal answer while live checkout is disabled.
- `403` — The identity is valid but lacks the required role or scope for this operation.
- `404` — The resource does not exist in this organization. Another tenant's ID answers the same 404 — the API never confirms that it exists elsewhere.
- `409` — The same key was used for a different purchase.

**Example**

```sh
curl -s -XPOST https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/$ORG/billing/purchases/pass -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Organization-Id: $ORG" -H "Idempotency-Key: $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'
```

## Operations

**Response `200`**

- `items` (object[]) — One entry per active alert, with its kind, severity and what to do about it.

**Errors**

- `401` — No session, no API key, or the credential does not resolve to this organization.
- `403` — The identity is valid but lacks the required role or scope for this operation.
- `404` — The resource does not exist in this organization. Another tenant's ID answers the same 404 — the API never confirms that it exists elsewhere.

**Example**

```sh
curl -s https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/$ORG/operations -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Organization-Id: $ORG"
```

### `POST /api/organizations/:organization_id/operations`

Re-observe alerts, quota and global capacity right now.

The GET reads what was last stored; this goes and looks again. Same distinction as domain verification.

- **URL:** `https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/:organization_id/operations`
- **Auth:** `organization_admin` — Human organization member with the required role; API keys cannot manage credentials or membership.

**Path parameters**

- `organization_id` (string, required) — Active organization ID. It must match the organization your session header or API key resolves to.

**Body example**

```json
{}
```

**Response `200`**

Structure: `Operations`.

- `alerts` (object[]) — Current alerts, each with a kind, a severity and what to do.
- `billing` (object) — Quota position at the time of the observation.
- `capacity` (object) — Conservative SES and SNS capacity observations.

**Errors**

- `401` — No session, no API key, or the credential does not resolve to this organization.
- `403` — The identity is valid but lacks the required role or scope for this operation.
- `404` — The resource does not exist in this organization. Another tenant's ID answers the same 404 — the API never confirms that it exists elsewhere.

**Example**

```sh
curl -s -XPOST https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/$ORG/operations -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Organization-Id: $ORG" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'
```

### `GET /api/metrics`

Last-7-day metrics for the operator dashboard; with the token, payments come along.

Without credentials it returns product usage: deliveries per day and organization totals. With `METRICS_TOKEN` as Bearer it adds `payments` — x402 settled on Base mainnet only.

- **URL:** `https://commsharbor.com/api/metrics`
- **Auth:** `none` — Public endpoint. No tenant data is returned.

**Headers**

- `Authorization` (string) — `Bearer <METRICS_TOKEN>` to include the financial block; a wrong token is 401.

**Response `200`**

Structure: `Metricas`.

- `app` (string) — Product name.
- `today` (string) — Reference day (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD).
- `today_visits` (int) — Interface visits counted today.
- `today_contacts` (int, optional) — Contact messages today. Only with `METRICS_TOKEN`: contact counts never leave without the token.
- `days` (object[]) — One row per day of the window, with each metric's count.
- `usage` (object) — `entregas`: deliveries per day — real product usage, not catalog load.
- `accounts` (object) — `organizacoes`: total organizations registered.
- `financeiro` (object, optional) — Day aggregate: `hoje_usd`, `hoje_count`, `rede`. Only with `METRICS_TOKEN`: money never leaves without the token; the full series is `payments`.
- `payments` (object, optional) — x402 financial summary; METRICS_TOKEN only.

**Errors**

- `401` — Wrong operator token.
- `503` — Worker without METRICS_TOKEN configured.

**Example**

```sh
curl -s https://commsharbor.com/api/metrics -H "Authorization: Bearer $METRICS_TOKEN"
```

### `GET /api/organizations/:organization_id/data-exports/:export_id`

`application/json` as an attachment, with the organization's data.


### `GET /api/organizations/:organization_id/deletion-requests`

Read the latest erasure request and where it is in the grace period.

`status: "none"` means no erasure was ever requested — the resource always answers, so a client never has to interpret a 404 as "nothing scheduled".

- **URL:** `https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/:organization_id/deletion-requests`
- **Auth:** `organization_admin` — Human organization member with the required role; API keys cannot manage credentials or membership.

**Path parameters**

- `organization_id` (string, required) — Active organization ID. It must match the organization your session header or API key resolves to.

**Response `200`**

Structure: `Deletion`.

- `id` (string, may be null) — Deletion request ID.
- `status` (string) — Where the request stands.
- `scheduled_for` (string, may be null) — When erasure runs, after the grace period (UTC).
- `requested_by` (string, may be null) — Who scheduled it.

**Errors**

- `401` — No session, no API key, or the credential does not resolve to this organization.
- `403` — The identity is valid but lacks the required role or scope for this operation.
- `404` — The resource does not exist in this organization. Another tenant's ID answers the same 404 — the API never confirms that it exists elsewhere.

**Example**

```sh
curl -s https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/$ORG/deletion-requests -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Organization-Id: $ORG"
```

### `POST /api/organizations/:organization_id/deletion-requests`

Schedule the erasure of the organization, after a seven-day grace period.

The confirmation phrase must be exactly `delete <organization_id>` — typing the id is the point, so nobody erases the wrong tenant by clicking. After erasure only pseudonymous financial and audit evidence remains.

- **URL:** `https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/:organization_id/deletion-requests`
- **Auth:** `organization_admin` — Human organization member with the required role; API keys cannot manage credentials or membership.

**Path parameters**

- `organization_id` (string, required) — Active organization ID. It must match the organization your session header or API key resolves to.

**Body** (`application/json`)

- `confirmation` (string, required) — The exact phrase `delete <organization_id>`.

**Body example**

```json
{
  "confirmation": "delete org_…"
}
```

**Response `200`**

Structure: `Deletion`.

- `id` (string, may be null) — Deletion request ID.
- `status` (string) — Where the request stands.
- `scheduled_for` (string, may be null) — When erasure runs, after the grace period (UTC).
- `requested_by` (string, may be null) — Who scheduled it.

**Errors**

- `400` — The confirmation phrase does not match this organization exactly.
- `401` — No session, no API key, or the credential does not resolve to this organization.
- `403` — The identity is valid but lacks the required role or scope for this operation.
- `404` — The resource does not exist in this organization. Another tenant's ID answers the same 404 — the API never confirms that it exists elsewhere.
- `409` — An erasure is already scheduled.

**Example**

```sh
curl -s -XPOST https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/$ORG/deletion-requests -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Organization-Id: $ORG" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"confirmation":"delete $ORG"}'
```

### `POST /api/organizations/:organization_id/deletion-requests/:request_id/cancel`

Cancel a scheduled erasure while it is still inside the grace period.

That is what the seven days are for: after they pass, there is nothing left to cancel.

- **URL:** `https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/:organization_id/deletion-requests/:request_id/cancel`
- **Auth:** `organization_admin` — Human organization member with the required role; API keys cannot manage credentials or membership.

**Path parameters**

- `organization_id` (string, required) — Active organization ID. It must match the organization your session header or API key resolves to.
- `request_id` (string, required) — Deletion request ID from the deletion-requests resource.

**Body example**

```json
{}
```

**Response `200`**

Structure: `Deletion`.

- `id` (string, may be null) — Deletion request ID.
- `status` (string) — Where the request stands.
- `scheduled_for` (string, may be null) — When erasure runs, after the grace period (UTC).
- `requested_by` (string, may be null) — Who scheduled it.

**Errors**

- `401` — No session, no API key, or the credential does not resolve to this organization.
- `403` — The identity is valid but lacks the required role or scope for this operation.
- `404` — The resource does not exist in this organization. Another tenant's ID answers the same 404 — the API never confirms that it exists elsewhere.
- `409` — The erasure already ran, or the request was cancelled before.

**Example**

```sh
curl -s -XPOST https://commsharbor.com/api/organizations/$ORG/deletion-requests/$REQUEST/cancel -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Organization-Id: $ORG" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'
```

## Credit

### `POST /api/credito`

Top up prepaid credit: pay once with x402 and get the token that debits on any API of the house.

- **URL:** `https://commsharbor.com/api/credito`
- **Auth:** `none` — Public endpoint. No tenant data is returned.

**Query**

- `usd` (int, required) — Package: 1, 5, 10 ou 25 dollars.

**Response `200`**

- `token` (string) — Bearer token for the balance (`cred_…`). Shown ONCE — it cannot be recovered.
- `saldo_usd` (string) — Credited balance.
- `guarde` (string) — Warning that the token is the bearer of the credit.
- `usar` (string) — How to present the token on paid routes.
- `saldo_em` (string) — Where to check balance and statement.

**Errors**

- `400` — Package outside the list (1, 5, 10 ou 25).
- `402` — Unpaid — the body carries the x402 `accepts[]`.

**Example**

```sh
curl -s -XPOST 'https://commsharbor.com/api/credito?usd=10'
```

### `GET /api/credito`

Credit balance and statement — the latest movements, without returning the token.

- **URL:** `https://commsharbor.com/api/credito`
- **Auth:** `credito` — Prepaid credit token in `Authorization: Bearer cred_…` (or the `X-Credito` header). Not an account: it is a bearer of balance.

**Response `200`**

- `saldo_micros` (int) — Balance in micro-dollars (1e-6 USD).
- `saldo_usd` (string) — Formatted balance.
- `criado_em` (string) — When the credit was opened.
- `movimentos` (object[]) — Recent credits and debits, with product and resource.

**Errors**

- `401` — No token, or unknown token.

**Example**

```sh
curl -s https://commsharbor.com/api/credito -H 'Authorization: Bearer cred_…'
```

## Structures

### `ApiIndex`

The self-describing index of the whole API.

- `name` (string) — Product name.
- `description` (string) — What the product does, in one sentence.
- `build` (string) — Deployed commit.
- `environment` (string) — Which environment answered: `production`, `staging` or `local`.
- `base_url` (string) — Origin this API is served from.
- `docs` (object) — Links to llms.txt, llms-full.txt, openapi.json, the MCP endpoint and the human UI.
- `auth` (object) — Every authentication mode and how to obtain it.
- `endpoints` (object[]) — Every endpoint with method, path, auth, absolute URL and what it returns.
- `mcp` (object) — Remote MCP endpoint and transport.
- `mcp_tools` (string[]) — Name of every MCP tool.

### `Health`

Liveness and the commit currently serving. Smoke tests wait for their own deploy here instead of racing edge propagation.

- `ok` (bool) — Always true when the Worker answers.
- `app` (string) — Product name.
- `build` (string) — Deployed commit; CI passes the short SHA at deploy time.
- `environment` (string) — Which environment answered.
- `timestamp` (string) — Response time (UTC, ISO-8601).

### `User`

The person behind the session.

- `id` (string) — User ID.
- `email` (string) — Email address confirmed by one-time code.

### `Ok`

Write confirmation for an operation with no body of its own.

- `ok` (bool) — Always true — failures arrive as a 4xx/5xx status, never as `ok:false`.

### `Profile`

Personal preferences. They belong to the person, not to any organization.

- `display_name` (string, may be null) — Name shown in the interface.
- `locale` (string, may be null) — Preferred language, e.g. `en` or `pt-br`.

### `Organization`

A tenant. Every piece of customer data in this product is scoped to exactly one.

- `id` (string) — Organization ID, used in every tenant route.
- `name` (string) — Display name.
- `sending_domain` (string, may be null) — Domain the organization sends from.
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC, ISO-8601).

### `Identity`

Who the current credential resolves to. Read this before a write when you are not sure which organization is active.

- `kind` (string) — How the identity was resolved.
- `organizationId` (string) — The active organization.
- `userId` (string, optional) — The person, when a session is in play.
- `email` (string, optional) — The person's e-mail, on a session.
- `sessionId` (string, optional) — Session identifier, on a session.
- `role` (string, optional) — Role inside that organization; sessions only.
- `organization` (object, optional) — `{ id, name, slug }` of the active organization; sessions only.
- `apiKeyId` (string, optional) — Which key answered, on an API key.
- `scopes` (string[], optional) — Granted scopes; present on an API key, which carries its own narrower set.

### `Membership`

One person's place in one organization.

- `organization_id` (string) — The organization.
- `user_id` (string) — The member.
- `role` (string) — What the member may do.
- `created_at` (string) — When the membership started (UTC).

### `Invitation`

An invitation into an existing organization. The token is revealed once, at creation, and never listed again.

- `id` (string) — Invitation ID.
- `email` (string) — Who is being invited.
- `role` (string) — Role the invitation grants.
- `expires_at` (string) — When the invitation stops working (UTC).
- `invitation_token` (string, optional) — The invitation token. Present only on the response that created it.
- `token_notice` (string, optional) — Reminder that the token is shown once.

### `ApiKey`

A scoped machine credential. It determines its own organization and rejects a conflicting header.

- `id` (string) — API key ID, used to revoke it.
- `name` (string) — Label chosen at creation.
- `scopes` (string[]) — What this key may do, e.g. `crm:read`, `messages:send`.
- `prefix` (string) — Token prefix, so a key can be recognised in a list.
- `last_used_at` (string, may be null) — When the key last answered; null if never.
- `revoked_at` (string, may be null) — When it was revoked; null while it is still valid.
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC).
- `token` (string, optional) — The key itself. Present only on the response that created it — it is never shown again.

### `PageCamel<AuditEvent>`

The same listing with the cursor in camelCase. Older resources ship it this way and the name is kept because changing it would break clients already reading it.

- `items` (AuditEvent[]) — The records on this page. → see `AuditEvent` under **Structures**.
- `nextCursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `AuditEvent`

One append-only record of something that happened in the organization. Audit is never rewritten.

- `id` (string) — Event ID.
- `action` (string) — What happened, e.g. `api_key.created`.
- `actor_user_id` (string, may be null) — Who did it; null when the actor was a key or the system.
- `target` (string, may be null) — What it happened to.
- `metadata` (object) — Extra context for this action. Never contains recipient PII.
- `created_at` (string) — When it happened (UTC).

### `Lista<Domain>`

A complete, unpaginated collection — used where the set is bounded by design.

- `items` (Domain[]) — Every record in the collection. → see `Domain` under **Structures**.

### `Domain`

A sending domain. State is only ever what was OBSERVED at SES and DNS — this product does not infer it.

- `id` (string) — Domain ID.
- `domain` (string) — The domain itself, e.g. `example.com`.
- `status` (string) — Last observed state.
- `dkim_tokens` (string[]) — CNAME records to publish for DKIM.
- `dmarc` (object, may be null) — DMARC policy observed at the domain.
- `mail_from` (object, may be null) — Custom MAIL FROM subdomain and its observed state.
- `last_observed_at` (string, may be null) — When SES and DNS were last actually checked (UTC).
- `created_at` (string) — Registration time (UTC).

### `Provisioning`

The idempotent SES provisioning queued for a domain. Asking twice does not provision twice.

- `queued` (bool) — Whether this call enqueued provisioning work.
- `job_id` (string, may be null) — The provisioning job, when one was created.

### `Delivery`

One queued message. It never carries the recipient address or the body — that is deliberate, not an omission.

- `id` (string) — Delivery ID.
- `status` (string) — Delivery state, authoritative in D1.
- `domain_id` (string) — Domain it was sent from.
- `template_id` (string, may be null) — Template used.
- `template_version` (int, may be null) — Immutable template version used.
- `ses_message_id` (string, may be null) — SES MessageId, for correlating with AWS.
- `created_at` (string) — When it was queued (UTC).

### `Capacity`

What is left to send. The bootstrap global cap always prevails over any tenant allowance.

- `remaining` (int) — Sends still available to this organization.
- `global_remaining` (int) — Sends still available across the whole platform this month.
- `hard_cap` (int) — The global monthly cap on real recipients. Nothing raises it.

### `Dispatch`

What actually happened to the queue message behind this send.

- `queued` (bool) — Whether a Queue message was produced.
- `job_id` (string, may be null) — Dispatch job ID, when one was created.

### `Lista<Delivery>`

A complete, unpaginated collection — used where the set is bounded by design.

- `items` (Delivery[]) — Every record in the collection. → see `Delivery` under **Structures**.

### `Lista<DeliveryEvent>`

A complete, unpaginated collection — used where the set is bounded by design.

- `items` (DeliveryEvent[]) — Every record in the collection. → see `DeliveryEvent` under **Structures**.

### `DeliveryEvent`

A normalized SES feedback event. Open and Click are ADDITIVE — they never overwrite delivery state.

- `id` (string) — Event ID.
- `event_type` (string) — What SES reported.
- `occurred_at` (string) — When SES says it happened (UTC).
- `detail` (object) — Normalized detail for this event type, without recipient PII.

### `Page<Contact>`

Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

- `items` (Contact[]) — The records on this page. → see `Contact` under **Structures**.
- `next_cursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `Contact`

A person in the tenant CRM. Marketing consent is a separate resource — being in the CRM is not permission to email.

- `id` (string) — Contact ID.
- `email` (string) — Email address, normalized and never truncated.
- `first_name` (string, may be null) — Given name.
- `last_name` (string, may be null) — Family name.
- `company_id` (string, may be null) — Company this contact belongs to.
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC).
- `updated_at` (string, may be null) — Last change (UTC).
- `url` (string) — Absolute URL of this contact — agents never build the path by hand.

### `Page<Company>`

Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

- `items` (Company[]) — The records on this page. → see `Company` under **Structures**.
- `next_cursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `Company`

An organization in the tenant CRM — a customer of the customer, not a tenant of this product.

- `id` (string) — Company ID.
- `name` (string) — Company name.
- `domain` (string, may be null) — Primary domain.
- `website` (string, may be null) — Website URL.
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC).
- `updated_at` (string, may be null) — Last change (UTC).
- `url` (string) — Absolute URL of this company.

### `Page<Pipeline>`

Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

- `items` (Pipeline[]) — The records on this page. → see `Pipeline` under **Structures**.
- `next_cursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `Pipeline`

A named sequence of stages that deals move through.

- `id` (string) — Pipeline ID.
- `name` (string) — Pipeline name.
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC).
- `url` (string) — Absolute URL of this pipeline.

### `Page<Deal>`

Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

- `items` (Deal[]) — The records on this page. → see `Deal` under **Structures**.
- `next_cursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `Deal`

An opportunity moving through a pipeline. Money is stored in minor units to avoid float rounding.

- `id` (string) — Deal ID.
- `title` (string) — What the deal is.
- `pipeline_id` (string) — Pipeline the deal lives in.
- `stage_id` (string) — Current stage.
- `status` (string) — Where it stands.
- `value_minor` (int, may be null) — Value in the currency's minor unit — cents, not dollars.
- `currency` (string, may be null) — ISO 4217 code for `value_minor`.
- `contact_id` (string, may be null) — Main contact on the deal.
- `company_id` (string, may be null) — Company on the deal.
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC).
- `updated_at` (string, may be null) — Last change (UTC).
- `url` (string) — Absolute URL of this deal.

### `Page<Activity>`

Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

- `items` (Activity[]) — The records on this page. → see `Activity` under **Structures**.
- `next_cursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `Activity`

Something that happened with a contact, company or deal — a note, a call, a meeting.

- `id` (string) — Activity ID.
- `activity_type` (string) — What kind of activity it was, e.g. `note`, `call`, `meeting`.
- `note` (string) — The text of the activity.
- `deal_id` (string, may be null) — Deal it refers to.
- `contact_id` (string, may be null) — Contact it refers to.
- `company_id` (string, may be null) — Company it refers to.
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC).
- `url` (string) — Absolute URL of this activity.

### `Page<Task>`

Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

- `items` (Task[]) — The records on this page. → see `Task` under **Structures**.
- `next_cursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `Task`

Work someone still has to do, inside the tenant CRM.

- `id` (string) — Task ID.
- `title` (string) — What has to be done.
- `status` (string) — Current state.
- `due_at` (string, may be null) — When it is due (UTC).
- `assignee_user_id` (string, may be null) — Member responsible for it.
- `deal_id` (string, may be null) — Deal the task belongs to.
- `contact_id` (string, may be null) — Contact the task belongs to.
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC).
- `updated_at` (string, may be null) — Last change (UTC).
- `url` (string) — Absolute URL of this task.

### `Page<Stage>`

Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

- `items` (Stage[]) — The records on this page. → see `Stage` under **Structures**.
- `next_cursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `Stage`

One step of a pipeline. Stages belong to a pipeline and are addressed under it.

- `id` (string) — Stage ID.
- `pipeline_id` (string) — Pipeline this stage belongs to.
- `name` (string) — Stage name, e.g. `Proposal`.
- `position` (int) — Order within the pipeline, lowest first.
- `probability` (int, may be null) — Chance of winning at this stage, 0 to 100.
- `url` (string) — Absolute URL of this stage.

### `Page<Lead>`

Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

- `items` (Lead[]) — The records on this page. → see `Lead` under **Structures**.
- `next_cursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `Lead`

A prospective ORGANIZATION in the platform CRM. This is our own pipeline about tenants — it is not tenant data, and it is only reachable with an explicit platform grant.

- `id` (string) — Lead ID.
- `email` (string) — Contact email for the lead.
- `name` (string) — Who to talk to.
- `company_name` (string, may be null) — Name of the prospective organization.
- `source` (string, may be null) — Where the lead came from, e.g. `manual`.
- `stage` (string) — Where the lead is in our own funnel, e.g. `new`.
- `organization_id` (string, may be null) — The organization this lead became, once it converted.
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC).
- `updated_at` (string, may be null) — Last change (UTC).
- `url` (string) — Absolute URL of this lead.

### `Page<PlatformTask>`

Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

- `items` (PlatformTask[]) — The records on this page. → see `PlatformTask` under **Structures**.
- `next_cursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `PlatformTask`

Work on a platform lead. Same idea as a CRM task, different subject: this one is about a prospective tenant, not about a tenant's customer.

- `id` (string) — Task ID.
- `title` (string) — What has to be done.
- `status` (string) — Current state.
- `lead_id` (string, may be null) — Lead the task belongs to.
- `due_at` (string, may be null) — When it is due (UTC).
- `assignee_user_id` (string, may be null) — Who is responsible.
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC).
- `updated_at` (string, may be null) — Last change (UTC).
- `url` (string) — Absolute URL of this task.

### `Page<PlatformActivity>`

Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

- `items` (PlatformActivity[]) — The records on this page. → see `PlatformActivity` under **Structures**.
- `next_cursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `PlatformActivity`

Something that happened with a platform lead — our note about a prospective tenant.

- `id` (string) — Activity ID.
- `activity_type` (string) — What kind of activity it was, e.g. `note`.
- `note` (string) — The text of the activity.
- `lead_id` (string) — Lead it refers to.
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC).
- `url` (string) — Absolute URL of this activity.

### `Marketing`

Consent and preference for one contact. Recording consent NEVER restores a previous unsubscribe — that asymmetry is the point.

- `marketing_enabled` (bool) — Whether marketing may be sent to this contact right now.
- `basis` (string, may be null) — Why sending is allowed.
- `source` (string, may be null) — Where the consent came from, e.g. a signup form.
- `captured_at` (string, may be null) — When consent was captured (UTC).
- `unsubscribed_at` (string, may be null) — When the contact unsubscribed; null when they never did.

### `PreferenceToken`

Signed URLs for the preference centre and one-click unsubscribe, plus the headers to put in the message.

- `api_url` (string) — Machine-readable preference endpoint.
- `preferences_url` (string) — Human preference page.
- `unsubscribe_url` (string) — RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe endpoint.
- `marketing_headers` (object) — `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post`, ready to add to the message.

### `PreferenceState`

What the signed capability reveals. No login, and no email address is exposed.

- `marketing_enabled` (bool) — Whether marketing may be sent.
- `unsubscribed_at` (string, may be null) — When the contact unsubscribed.
- `expires_at` (string) — When this capability stops working (UTC).

### `Send`

The result of queueing one message. `replayed` true means an equivalent Idempotency-Key already existed and NO second message was produced.

- `delivery` (Delivery) — The delivery record. → see `Delivery` under **Structures**.
- `capacity` (Capacity) — What is left after this send. → see `Capacity` under **Structures**.
- `dispatch` (Dispatch) — The queue work behind it. → see `Dispatch` under **Structures**.
- `replayed` (bool) — True when this was a replay of an earlier identical request.

### `Page<ContactImport>`

Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

- `items` (ContactImport[]) — The records on this page. → see `ContactImport` under **Structures**.
- `next_cursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `ContactImport`

A CSV import of contacts, with the consent declaration that made it legal to import them.

- `id` (string) — Import ID.
- `status` (string) — Where the import stands.
- `rows` (int) — Rows found in the CSV.
- `accepted` (int) — Rows that will be imported.
- `rejected` (int) — Rows rejected, with reasons in the errors listing.
- `basis` (string) — Declared consent basis for every row.
- `file_id` (string, may be null) — Stored file, downloadable for seven days.
- `created_at` (string) — Upload time (UTC).

### `ImportError`

One rejected row, addressed by line number so it can be fixed in the source file.

- `row` (int) — 1-based row number in the uploaded CSV.
- `code` (string) — Why it was rejected, e.g. `invalid_email`.
- `message` (string) — The reason in a sentence.

### `Page<ImportError>`

Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

- `items` (ImportError[]) — The records on this page. → see `ImportError` under **Structures**.
- `next_cursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `Page<Suppression>`

Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

- `items` (Suppression[]) — The records on this page. → see `Suppression` under **Structures**.
- `next_cursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `Suppression`

A recipient that must not be emailed. Suppressions are checked BEFORE quota and before any queue work.

- `id` (string) — Suppression ID.
- `scope` (string) — How far it reaches.
- `reason` (string) — Why it exists, e.g. `bounce`, `complaint`, `manual`.
- `contact_id` (string, may be null) — CRM contact it matches, when known.
- `created_at` (string) — When it was added (UTC).

### `Page<Audience>`

Cursor-paginated listing. A null cursor means this was the last page.

- `items` (Audience[]) — The records on this page. → see `Audience` under **Structures**.
- `next_cursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `Audience`

Who a campaign goes to: a static list or a saved segment with an allowlisted filter.

- `id` (string) — Audience ID.
- `name` (string) — Audience name.
- `kind` (string) — How membership is decided.
- `filter` (object, may be null) — The saved filter, for `saved_segment`. Only allowlisted fields are accepted.
- `member_count` (int, may be null) — Contacts currently in the audience.
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC).

### `PageCamel<Template>`

The same listing with the cursor in camelCase. Older resources ship it this way and the name is kept because changing it would break clients already reading it.

- `items` (Template[]) — The records on this page. → see `Template` under **Structures**.
- `nextCursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `Template`

An email template as a draft. Published versions are immutable and live in their own resource.

- `id` (string) — Template ID.
- `name` (string) — Template name.
- `message_type` (string) — What it may be used for.
- `subject` (string) — Subject line, with `{{variable}}` placeholders.
- `variables` (object[]) — Typed variables the template declares: name, type and whether it is required.
- `blocks` (object[]) — Canonical content blocks. Imported HTML is converted into these.
- `status` (string) — Draft state.
- `latest_version` (int, may be null) — Highest published version; null while never published.
- `updated_at` (string, may be null) — Last change (UTC).

### `TemplateVersion`

A published version. Immutable and identified by the hash of its content — republishing identical content does not create a new one.

- `version` (int) — Version number, increasing.
- `content_hash` (string) — Hash of the compiled content; it is the version's identity.
- `subject` (string) — Subject at this version.
- `published_at` (string) — Publication time (UTC).

### `Lista<TemplateVersion>`

A complete, unpaginated collection — used where the set is bounded by design.

- `items` (TemplateVersion[]) — Every record in the collection. → see `TemplateVersion` under **Structures**.

### `TemplatePreview`

A draft compiled and rendered safely, without publishing anything.

- `subject` (string) — Subject with variables applied.
- `html` (string) — Rendered HTML.
- `text` (string) — Plain-text alternative.
- `warnings` (string[]) — What was stripped or would not render — active content, forms, unsafe URLs.

### `TemplateExport`

The latest published version in every form it exists.

- `template_id` (string) — ID of the exported template.
- `version` (int) — Exported version number.
- `subject` (string) — Subject at that version.
- `html` (string) — Compiled HTML.
- `text` (string) — Plain-text alternative.
- `mjml` (string) — MJML source of the compiled blocks.
- `content_hash` (string) — Hash identifying the version.

### `PageCamel<Campaign>`

The same listing with the cursor in camelCase. Older resources ship it this way and the name is kept because changing it would break clients already reading it.

- `items` (Campaign[]) — The records on this page. → see `Campaign` under **Structures**.
- `nextCursor` (string, may be null) — Cursor for the next page; null when there are no more.

### `Campaign`

A marketing send to an audience. Launching freezes the eligible recipients exactly once — the frozen set is what gets sent, no matter what changes afterwards.

- `id` (string) — Campaign ID.
- `name` (string) — Campaign name.
- `status` (string) — Where the campaign is.
- `domain_id` (string) — Domain it sends from.
- `audience_id` (string) — Audience it goes to.
- `template_id` (string) — Published marketing template used.
- `template_version` (int) — Frozen template version.
- `scheduled_for` (string, may be null) — When it is scheduled, in the organization's timezone.
- `frozen_recipients` (int, may be null) — How many recipients were frozen at launch.
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC).

### `CampaignReport`

Campaign reconciliation: what was delivered and what came back. Counts only — no recipient data.

- `campaign` (Campaign) — The campaign being reported on. → see `Campaign` under **Structures**.
- `deliveries` (object) — Delivery counts by state.
- `events` (object) — Normalized feedback counts by event type.

### `MessagingSettings`

Timezone and marketing pause state. A reputation or SES tenant risk pauses marketing automatically, and resuming requires a healthy observation first.

- `timezone` (string) — IANA timezone used to schedule campaigns, e.g. `America/Sao_Paulo`.
- `marketing_state` (string) — Whether marketing may go out.
- `paused_reason` (string, may be null) — Why marketing was paused, when it was.

### `Lista<Webhook>`

A complete, unpaginated collection — used where the set is bounded by design.

- `items` (Webhook[]) — Every record in the collection. → see `Webhook` under **Structures**.

### `Webhook`

An HTTPS endpoint that receives delivery events. The signing secret is revealed once, at creation.

- `id` (string) — Webhook ID.
- `url` (string) — HTTPS destination.
- `event_types` (string[]) — Which events are delivered to it.
- `status` (string) — Whether it is receiving.
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC).
- `secret` (string, optional) — Signing secret for timestamped HMAC-SHA256. Present only on the response that created it.

### `BillingPublic`

The public billing view: catalog, x402 configuration and whether signup is invite-only.

- `catalog` (BillingCatalog) — Plans and prices in force. → see `BillingCatalog` under **Structures**.
- `payment` (PlanoX402) — x402 configuration: network, asset, facilitator and where to pay. → see `PlanoX402` under **Structures**.
- `invite_only` (bool) — Whether new organizations require an invitation.

### `BillingTenant`

What THIS organization is entitled to, and how close it is to running out.

- `catalog` (BillingCatalog) — Plans and prices in force. → see `BillingCatalog` under **Structures**.
- `state` (object) — Current entitlement: what is active, how many sends remain and when it expires.
- `warning` (object, may be null) — Expiration or exhaustion warning, when one applies.
- `payment` (PlanoX402) — x402 configuration for paying. → see `PlanoX402` under **Structures**.

### `Operations`

Operational alerts for the organization — DLQ, backlog, worker and SNS failures, reputation, paused sending, quota and SES/SNS cost capacity. Never contains recipient PII.

- `alerts` (object[]) — Current alerts, each with a kind, a severity and what to do.
- `billing` (object) — Quota position at the time of the observation.
- `capacity` (object) — Conservative SES and SNS capacity observations.

### `Lista<DataExport>`

A complete, unpaginated collection — used where the set is bounded by design.

- `items` (DataExport[]) — Every record in the collection. → see `DataExport` under **Structures**.

### `DataExport`

A tenant-scoped JSON export, retained for seven days.

- `id` (string) — Export ID.
- `status` (string) — Where the export stands.
- `expires_at` (string) — When the file is deleted (UTC).
- `created_at` (string) — Creation time (UTC).

### `Deletion`

A scheduled tenant erasure. It waits seven days, and what survives is pseudonymous financial and audit evidence only.

- `id` (string, may be null) — Deletion request ID.
- `status` (string) — Where the request stands.
- `scheduled_for` (string, may be null) — When erasure runs, after the grace period (UTC).
- `requested_by` (string, may be null) — Who scheduled it.

### `Metricas`

7-day operator dashboard. `payments` only appears with the token and only on Base mainnet.

- `app` (string) — Product name.
- `today` (string) — Reference day (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD).
- `today_visits` (int) — Interface visits counted today.
- `today_contacts` (int, optional) — Contact messages today. Only with `METRICS_TOKEN`: contact counts never leave without the token.
- `days` (object[]) — One row per day of the window, with each metric's count.
- `usage` (object) — `entregas`: deliveries per day — real product usage, not catalog load.
- `accounts` (object) — `organizacoes`: total organizations registered.
- `financeiro` (object, optional) — Day aggregate: `hoje_usd`, `hoje_count`, `rede`. Only with `METRICS_TOKEN`: money never leaves without the token; the full series is `payments`.
- `payments` (object, optional) — x402 financial summary; METRICS_TOKEN only.

### `BillingCatalog`

Plans and prices, versioned. Nothing here auto-renews — a pass or a top-up is bought once and runs out.

- `version` (string) — Catalog version, so a client can tell prices changed.
- `trial` (object) — What a new organization gets for free.
- `pass` (object) — The paid pass: what it grants and what it costs.
- `topup` (object) — One-off send top-up: size and price.
- `checkout_live` (bool) — Whether live checkout is enabled. While false, a purchase returns an x402 challenge.
- `global_recipient_hard_cap` (int) — Real recipients per month across the whole platform. This always prevails.
- `auto_renew` (bool) — Always false — nothing here renews by itself.

### `PlanoX402`

x402 payment configuration in force. Comes from `planPublic` and is the same across the products.

- `provider` (string) — Always `x402` — the only billing protocol accepted.
- `mode` (string) — Seller mode: `live` charges for real, `dev` lets calls through unpaid.
- `network` (string) — USDC network: `base` in production, `base-sepolia` in staging.
- `chain_id` (int) — EVM chain ID of the network above, so the wallet signs on the right chain.
- `pay_to` (string, may be null) — Address that receives the payment.
- `homolog` (bool) — Staging seam on: the loop can be closed without spending USDC.
- `dev` (bool) — Development mode: the 402 is simulated.
- `dev_gate` (string, may be null) — How dev mode is unlocked, when it exists.
- `facilitator` (string) — URL of the facilitator that verifies and settles the payment.
- `asset` (string) — Accepted currency — always `USDC`.
- `asset_address` (string) — USDC contract on the network above.
- `faucet` (string, may be null) — Test-USDC faucet; only on base-sepolia.
- `wallets` (object) — Links to wallets that speak x402 (metamask, coinbase, base_app).
